title: Meta and SpaceX show two ways to finance the AI compute buildout
dek: Meta proposed large equity issuance while SpaceX disclosed a GPU leasing commitment—different capital structures for costly accelerator capacity.
evidence: Meta offering announcement and SpaceX deal reporting; proposed programs are not committed funding
takeaway: Model compute economics with lease obligations, delivery timelines and financing terms rather than raw announced capex.

sections.title: Capital structures

bullets.detail: Meta announced approximately $35B of underwritten equity offerings and proposed a future $60B at-the-market program; the latter was not yet established and may never occur.
SpaceX disclosed an approximately $40B commitment for Apollo-managed entities to purchase and lease GPU/server equipment, with leases beginning as tranches are delivered.

paragraphs: Meta: Meta announced approximately $35B of underwritten equity offerings and proposed a future $60B at-the-market program; the latter was not yet established and may never occur.
SpaceX: SpaceX disclosed an approximately $40B commitment for Apollo-managed entities to purchase and lease GPU/server equipment, with leases beginning as tranches are delivered.

sections.title: Analysis

bullets.detail: Equity issuance dilutes ownership; equipment finance leases create ongoing obligations tied to asset life and delivery. Announcement totals should not be conflated with cash spent today.
Compare fleet utilization, depreciation, financing cost, residual hardware value, networking and power readiness before inferring a unit cost per token.
